A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VILAMP study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, VideoNIAH experiments, redundancy analyses, ablations, and computational-efficiency and hyperparameter studies.

after.justification: v4 retains those original results and adds VILAMP evaluations on grounding and action-recognition tasks in Tables 3–4.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same differential keyframe selection, feature merging, two-stream connectors, and training objective. The new tasks use the existing method without a documented algorithmic modification.

E1.justification: v4 substantially broadens evaluation beyond the retained five video-QA benchmarks and VideoNIAH. Section 5.4 adds QVHighlights grounding and action recognition on ActivityNet, Something-Something V2, and UCF-101.

E2.justification: New Table 4 adds published AdaFrame results on ActivityNet and MGSampler results on Something-Something V2 and UCF-101. Comparator membership in the original benchmark, VideoNIAH, ablation, and efficiency comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: The added tasks introduce distinct evaluation designs: annotated-keyframe retrieval measured by Hit@1/5/10/30, and action classification reformulated as multiple-choice testing, reported as zero-shot with mAP or accuracy. Existing experiments retain their protocols. The new action-recognition passage does not establish matched testing conditions with the published baselines.

E4.justification: The QVHighlights analysis directly checks whether DKS selections recover annotated query-relevant keyframes, adding a targeted diagnostic of selection quality. Existing redundancy analyses, DKS/DFM ablations, keyframe-count study, and appendix hyperparameter sensitivities remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Existing statistical displays and reporting practices are retained. New Tables 3–4 provide point estimates without adding repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: New Table 3 reports QVHighlights Hit@1/5/10/30 of 26.1/47.3/60.0/83.2. Table 4 adds VILAMP results of 78.6 mAP on ActivityNet and 86.9%/97.6% accuracy on Something-Something V2/UCF-101, alongside sourced baseline results. These extend the empirical findings to new tasks; all matched original benchmark, ablation, efficiency, and sensitivity results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Equations 1–12, and algorithmic complexity reasoning are unchanged. No theorem or proof is added; the new Hit@k description explains an empirical metric.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same core claims about differential distillation, the DKS/DFM hierarchy, performance across five video benchmarks, and processing 10K frames on one GPU. The additional evaluations do not revise these headline contributions.

C2.justification: v4 interprets QVHighlights results as evidence that DKS captures query-relevant clips and suggests that pretrained general knowledge explains action-recognition transfer. These extend the applicability discussion; existing mechanism explanations and impact-related limitations are retained.

D1.justification: The abstract adds code/model access information. Appendix A.3 removes the stated 2.5M WebVid/InternVid sample contribution and omits HiREST from the training-data table while retaining it in the prose. These documentation changes do not establish that training changed; the main hyperparameters and hardware disclosures remain.

R1.justification: v4 adds six references supporting the new grounding/action benchmarks and AdaFrame/MGSampler comparisons. This modestly extends positioning toward action recognition and adaptive frame selection, while the existing related-work discussion and novelty framing remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 adds a localized discussion of other video tasks and acknowledgments, updates affiliations, corrects the conference edition, and replaces the template running header with the paper title. Most prose and the section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v4 adds two compact results tables, moves the unchanged Figure 5 from PDF page 5 to page 6, and repositions Algorithm 1. Existing figures retain their graphics; appendix Tables 3–4 become Tables 5–6 without substantive display changes.

improvement.justification: v4 adds useful direct evidence about keyframe selection and broader task applicability, plus code/model access information, while preserving the original study. The gain is limited: the multiple-choice action-recognition comparison lacks documented alignment with published baseline protocols, and Appendix A.3 loses sampling detail and becomes inconsistent about HiREST. These tradeoffs prevent the additions from establishing a substantial overall improvement.
